constitutional_basis: Article VIII (frozen criterion), Article XXVI (ACTUAL external solver), Article XXXII (strongest alternative tested)

experimental_design.purpose: Eliminate the alternative explanation that distributed wins merely because it retained more open conductance. Match obstruction fractions so both configurations lose the same fraction of total capacity.
experimental_design.experiment_A: 50% obstruction matched: Distributed (5/10 channels blocked, 0.2x flow per remaining channel, normal R) vs Single (1.0x flow, 2x R = 50% obstruction)
experimental_design.experiment_B: 90% obstruction matched: Distributed (1.0x flow through remaining channel, normal R — representing 1 of 10 channels carrying full load) vs Single (1.0x flow, 10x R = 90% obstruction)
experimental_design.frozen_criterion: Distributed inlet pressure < 50% of single inlet pressure at MATCHED obstruction. Frozen before execution.

experiment_A_50pct_matched.verdict: PASS — distributed is 13% of single, well below 50% threshold. 7.6x safer.

experiment_B_90pct_matched.verdict: PASS — distributed is 32% of single, below 50% threshold. 3.2x safer.

mechanism_verification.thesis: P-19's distributed architecture provides safety advantage BEYOND mere capacity retention. At matched obstruction fractions, distributed produces lower pressure than single.
mechanism_verification.svMultiPhysics_confirms: YES — at 50% matched obstruction, distributed is 7.6x safer. At 90% matched obstruction, distributed is 3.2x safer. The advantage DECREASES at higher obstruction (more channels blocked) but REMAINS significant.
mechanism_verification.key_finding: The distributed architecture's advantage is NOT just capacity retention. Even when both configurations lose the same fraction of total conductance, the distributed system produces lower pressure because: (1) flow is distributed across multiple parallel paths (lower per-path velocity = lower Poiseuille resistance), (2) remaining channels operate at normal resistance while the obstructed single channel has elevated resistance.
mechanism_verification.mechanism_verified: TRUE — at matched obstruction, distributed architecture is inherently safer, not just capacity-rich.

outcome: PASS — both matched-obstruction experiments confirm P-19's distributed advantage
label: MECHANISM_VERIFIED — matched-obstruction 3D test through svMultiPhysics confirms distributed architecture is inherently safer
what_this_proves: P-19's core mechanism is verified under controlled, matched-obstruction conditions. The R320 correction (unequal obstruction) is resolved — at matched 50% and 90% obstruction, distributed wins by 7.6x and 3.2x respectively. The advantage is architectural, not just capacity retention.
alternative_explanation_eliminated: R320 concern: 'distributed wins because it retained more conductance.' R321 result: at matched conductance loss (50%/50% and 90%/90%), distributed still wins. Alternative explanation eliminated.
